dimensions.assessment: Directly affects wildland firefighters employed by the Forest Service and the Department of the Interior.
dimensions.evidence: an employee of the Forest Service or the Department of the Interior who qualifies as a wildland firefighter

dimensions.assessment: Provides mandatory paid rest and recuperation leave after strenuous deployments and removes overtime payment caps for subsequent calendar years, offering substantial benefit changes for covered personnel.
dimensions.evidence: A covered employee may receive paid rest and recuperation leave following the completion of service

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes the transfer of not more than $5,000,000 of unobligated balances from specific accounts to continue base salary increases and premium pay.
dimensions.evidence: not more than $5,000,000 of the unobligated balances of amounts made available under the heading wildland fire management

dimensions.assessment: Amends title 5 of the United States Code to establish a new leave category and alters statutory limits on premium pay and overtime for firefighters.
dimensions.evidence: Subchapter II of chapter 63 of title 5, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent leave policies and lifts overtime caps for any calendar year thereafter, creating ongoing operational rules.
dimensions.evidence: by striking or 2022 or 2023 or 2024 and inserting or any calendar year thereafter

missing_information: Total number of Forest Service and Department of the Interior employees who will qualify as wildland firefighters under the updated definitions.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill creates paid rest and recuperation leave for federal wildland firefighters, authorizes specific fund transfers up to $5,000,000, and permanently waives certain overtime caps.
